tasks.title: Corrupt subscriber stores exit 2 with one escaped diagnostic and released locks
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, Behavior, Tests regressions 1-12 and controls 13-15 plus existing-suite controls, Docs, and Checks and completion evidence 1-13; Required behavior 1-6 (including 4a-4f); Performance impact; Security impact; Counterexamples. One change implements the CLI fix, its regression tests and both docs; fix and tests land in the same commit because of per-file coverage. Use the exact N/S/T/R test recipes, independent literal path expectations and the pending-WAL fixture P of check 4 in the current plan. P is external evidence only; retain exactly 12 regression tests plus 3 controls. Docs and the runSubscribers doc comment make no byte-equality claim for any class of inputs (Required behavior 4f); only fixture-named tests and PR evidence may state bytes. Preserve the store call sequence and base-relative store/sidecar state; byte equality and no-sidecar evidence is limited to the proven fixtures. Keep store format, protected store implementation, service startup, unsupported commands and other exit codes unchanged. Record actual pre-edit BASE; if both required valid executable delete invocations on N already return 2 there, request a hold instead of review. Evidence files, coverage config and harnesses stay outside the implementation checkout and are created/edited with file tools.

Executable N with probe@example.com and Absent@Example.com fails status 1 !== 2 and prints SQLiteError: file is not a database; public N and all five path cases throw SQLITE_NOTADB; S with each address throws SQLITE_CORRUPT during open; T and R with stored probe@example.com throw SQLITE_CORRUPT in deleteByEmail. Record names and reasons for every run. All three controls pass on BASE. Missing imports, setup errors and coverage failures are not acceptable red evidence.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts || exit "$?"; done
acceptance.expected: All three branch runs exit 0 with exactly 15 pass, 0 fail, covering Repository: notify Tests 1-15. Tests 1-2 spawn process.execPath with src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com and, on a fresh N, Absent@Example.com; environment is only PATH and PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE. Each exits 2, stdout is empty, stderr equals pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <file>: the file is corrupt or not a database followed by one newline. Tests 3-6 return exactly { lines: [that diagnostic without its final newline], code: 2 } for public N, S with each address and T with stored probe@example.com. Do not require T with an absent address to fail. Apply shared assertions C from the spec to cases 1-11: full byte equality, absent lock, directory listing exactly the fixture filename, immediate acquireLock(..., testLockDeps()).release(), and absence of argument/normalized addresses, sentinel, SQLite and stack frames. Fixtures use 50 rows and the exact page damage of the plan; no global or module mocks or test-only exports. Tests 7-11 use the five input names and literal shown names from the plan's path table: LF -> \u000a, CR -> \u000d, CRLF -> \u000d\u000a, literal backslash-n -> doubled backslash plus n, and U+2028/NEL/DEL/ESC -> \u2028/\u0085/\u007f/\u001b. Build expected strings from join(dir, literal shown name), never the escaping helper under test. The escape rule doubles backslash and replaces every Cc, U+2028 and U+2029 with \u plus four lowercase hex digits; no other change, quotes or raw line separators. Use Unicode property escapes with the u flag, not control-character ranges or JSON.stringify. Test 12 on R returns the fixed diagnostic/code 2, leaves no lock, and readdirSync is exactly the fixture filename with no WAL, SHM or journal; output has no address or sentinel. Header bytes 18/19 change from [1, 1] to [2, 2], big-endian counters at offsets 24 and 92 each increase by 1, and file length is unchanged. Restoring only offsets 18, 19, 24-27 and 92-95 from before makes after equal before. Do not assert byte equality for R: this is protected SubscriberStore.open behavior on BASE too. N and damaged WAL fixtures S/T retain complete byte equality. These fixture assertions are not a universal byte or sidecar guarantee; checkpoint failures after a committed delete are code-reading-only coverage. P is not a sixteenth test: it is separate check-4 evidence, proving that the close checkpoint can change the main file even when the delete fails before commit.

acceptance.command:
bun /tmp/notify-store-evidence/build.ts || exit 1
for fixture in N S T R P; do
  fixture_root="/tmp/notify-store-state/$fixture"
  base_status=0
  (cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE="$fixture_root/base/store.db" bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com) || base_status=$?
  branch_status=0
  env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE="$fixture_root/branch/store.db" bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com || branch_status=$?
  printf '%s base=%s branch=%s\n' "$fixture" "$base_status" "$branch_status"
  test "$base_status" -eq 1 && test "$branch_status" -eq 2 || exit 1
  cmp "$fixture_root/base/store.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db" || exit 1
  test "$(ls -A "$fixture_root/base")" = store.db && test "$(ls -A "$fixture_root/branch")" = store.db || exit 1
  ls -A "$fixture_root/base"
  ls -A "$fixture_root/branch"
  compare_status=0
  cmp_output=$(cmp -l "$fixture_root/original/store.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db") || compare_status=$?
  printf '%s original-vs-branch status=%s differing_bytes=' "$fixture" "$compare_status"
  printf '%s' "$cmp_output" | awk 'END { print NR }'
  case "$fixture" in
    R|P) test "$compare_status" -eq 1 || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$cmp_output" ;;
    *) test "$compare_status" -eq 0 || exit 1 ;;
  esac
  bun /tmp/notify-store-evidence/assert.ts "$fixture" "$fixture_root/original/store.db" "$fixture_root/branch/store.db" || exit 1
done
acceptance.expected: Create the external builder and independent artifact assertion script with file tools in their own /tmp/notify-store-evidence directory; neither is a notify change. Builder exits 0, builds one original directory per fixture N/S/T/R/P using exactly the plan's recipes and the protected SubscriberStore, and copies each original directory byte-identically into fresh base and branch directories under /tmp/notify-store-state/<fixture>. N/S/T/R originals contain only store.db. P recipe: build damaged WAL table fixture T in scratch W; open raw Database(W/store.db), set PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0, INSERT INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ('k', 'v'); while the connection is open, copy store.db and store.db-wal (not store.db-shm) into P/original, then process.exit(0) without closing. Use a separate builder subprocess for this step so the parent can continue. Builder verifies P/original listing exactly store.db and store.db-wal, nonempty WAL (observed 8272 bytes with page size 4096, not a portable assertion), then copies both files into P/base and P/branch. Every BASE invocation exits 1; T/R/P stderr names SQLITE_CORRUPT. Every branch invocation exits 2 with the fixed diagnostic and empty stdout. Retain stdout/stderr and record all statuses. For each of all five fixtures, base-vs-branch cmp exits 0 and both final listings equal exactly store.db: no WAL, SHM, journal or lock. Against originals, N/S/T cmp exits 0 with 0 differing bytes; R and P cmp exit 1. assert.ts exits 0 only when independent per-fixture assertions hold: N/S/T exact byte equality; R equal length, bytes 18/19 [1,1] -> [2,2], big-endian counters at 24 and 92 each +1, and restoring offsets 18,19,24-27,92-95 makes the buffers equal; P equal length but different main-file bytes (22 differing bytes observed in planning, not a required count). R cmp -l permits only one-based offsets 19/20,25-28,93-96, usually 19/20/28/96. Record all cmp statuses, actual differing-byte counts, offsets/values and directory listings in the PR body. P changes because close checkpoints earlier committed meta frames despite deleteByEmail failing before the delete commits; skipping close would violate 4b. The shell acceptance exits 0 only when these statuses and assertions hold. This is fixture-bound evidence for 4b/4e; other inputs are covered only by code review of the same store calls/order, with no class-wide byte or sidecar guarantee.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-base/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com)
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-branch/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
acceptance.expected: Prepare independent format-1 stores with SubscriberStore, close them, set PRAGMA user_version = 2 using raw Database connections, then close. On BASE and branch, the real-CLI control exits 2 with empty stdout and stderr exactly pulse-notify: PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE: the store has an unknown format followed by one newline. No .lock remains. Record both results; this carries the issue review's executable schema-version baseline control.

Exit 0 for full lint, typecheck and tests under normal committed coverage settings; the spec's literal branch count is 811 pass, 0 fail (796 on BASE). src/subscribers-cli.ts line coverage is at least 80 %, cognitive complexity at most 15 per function. Source fix and regression tests land together so per-file coverage stays green; include both docs in the same change. Report Bun 1.4.0. Do not substitute focused coverage runs for this gate.

Code review proves Required behavior 1-6, especially 4a-4f, and the Security impact checklist. Only instanceof SQLiteError with (errno & 0xff) in {11, 26} maps to the fixed code-2 diagnostic, including extended variants and errors at open, delete/its checkpoint or close. Keep argument/address validation before acquiring the lock or opening the store. Once acquired, lock release is guaranteed on success, handled/rethrown errors and close throws. Make exactly the same store calls as BASE in the same order: openExisting once, deleteByEmail once if a store was returned, then close once even after a delete error. Add no SQLite statement, pragma, second open, checkpoint, header pre-check, integrity scan, repair or store/sidecar file access. First error wins: if delete throws, attempt close and discard its error before classifying/rethrowing the delete error; if only close throws, classify/rethrow that error. Delete SQLITE_CORRUPT plus close SQLITE_IOERR gives code 2; delete SQLITE_BUSY plus close SQLITE_CORRUPT rethrows SQLITE_BUSY (executable exit 1). Other exceptions are rethrown. Preserve ConfigError/StartupError text, SUBSCRIBERS_USAGE, INVALID_ADDRESS_LINE and exports. Keep runSubscribers' doc comment accurate: corrupt store is exit 2, with no unconditional byte/sidecar or nothing-deleted promise. The result carries only the escaped configured path and fixed reason, never raw SQLite messages, file content, address, errno/code or stack. Review hostile file bytes, damaged rows, R, pending-WAL P, escaped paths, validation precedence, normalized/whitespace addresses and directory-path control. Store state is relative to BASE: damage found at a checkpoint after commit leaves the delete committed and can leave WAL/SHM, exactly as on BASE; exit 2 does not confirm whether the address was deleted. Byte and absent-sidecar evidence applies only to the named N/S/T/R/P fixtures built by the recipes: N/S/T unchanged, R exact header rewrite, P main file changed by close checkpoint with pending WAL removed; all five match BASE. Other inputs are covered only by the same-store-call-order review. Docs and the doc comment make no byte-equality claim for any class of inputs, even non-database files or damaged WAL stores detected before the delete commits (4f). Explicitly report close-throw lock release, first-error-wins and SQLITE_CORRUPT_* variants as code-reading-only coverage, same-call-order evidence as code reading plus the five-fixture comparison, and raw-path lock messages as a known limit. No changes outside the four allowed files.
Exit 1 with no output: both files hold only ASCII. Every non-ASCII test character is written as a Unicode escape, and test names hold only printable ASCII.

Both documents describe the exact pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <path>: the file is corrupt or not a database line, exit 2, escaped path, no address and released lock, matching the independent test literals. README adds one short sentence to the email-subscriptions paragraph and links docs/operation.md#subscriber-store; that sentence names only the code, line, escaping, privacy and lock release. The operator deletion bullet specifies backslash as \\ and Cc/U+2028/U+2029 as \uXXXX with four lowercase hex digits, no output line holds the address, released lock, no repair, and the same SQLite calls as any delete with no extra check or write. It says exit 2 does not confirm whether the address was deleted: damage found at a checkpoint after the delete commits leaves the deletion and can leave WAL/SHM, as on BASE. It lists what any run can change: opening sets WAL, so an externally switched rollback-journal file gets its header changed; closing writes earlier committed data waiting in <store>-wal into the main file and removes -wal. Advise keeping a copy of the damaged file and its -wal/-shm before running if needed, restoring from backup, then running subscribers delete <address> again. Neither docs file nor runSubscribers' doc comment makes a byte-equality claim for any class of inputs, including non-database files or damaged WAL stores whose damage is found before commit; neither promises no sidecar or nothing deleted. Fixture byte evidence stays in tests and the PR body only, explicitly naming N/S/T/R/P. Review the added sentences in context as well as the separate literal-count check; do not evade it with synonyms. No new command, repair or startup change; leave the service Exit codes table unchanged. Both docs are in the same change, agreeing with the plan and issue review's exact file set.

acceptance.command:
for file in README.md docs/operation.md src/subscribers-cli.ts; do
  case "$file" in
    README.md) expected_count=1 ;;
    docs/operation.md) expected_count=3 ;;
    src/subscribers-cli.ts) expected_count=0 ;;
  esac
  for revision in "$BASE" HEAD; do
    git cat-file -e "$revision:$file" || exit 1
    observed_count=$(git show "$revision:$file" | grep -oiE 'unchanged|not changed|byte for byte|no sidecar|nothing (was )?deleted' | wc -l)
    printf '%s %s count=%s expected=%s\n' "$revision" "$file" "$observed_count" "$expected_count"
    test "$observed_count" -eq "$expected_count" || exit 1
  done
done
acceptance.expected: Exit 0 after the last implementation commit. At both recorded BASE and HEAD, counts are literally README.md 1, docs/operation.md 3 and src/subscribers-cli.ts 0, independently measured on the planning base 3b000f2 and specified in check 8. Existing unrelated uses remain; no new forbidden wording appears. Inspect semantics too: the docs and runSubscribers doc comment make no byte-equality claim for any class of inputs and no nothing-deleted or no-sidecar promise. The PR body cites byte evidence only per named fixture. This command does not replace the preceding contextual docs review.

acceptance.command:
base_source_bytes=$(git cat-file -s "$BASE":src/subscribers-cli.ts) &&
branch_source_bytes=$(git cat-file -s HEAD:src/subscribers-cli.ts) &&
test "$base_source_bytes" -eq 1683 &&
source_byte_delta=$((branch_source_bytes - base_source_bytes)) &&
printf 'base_bytes=%s branch_bytes=%s delta_bytes=%s\n' "$base_source_bytes" "$branch_source_bytes" "$source_byte_delta" &&
awk -v delta="$source_byte_delta" 'BEGIN { printf "estimated_image_mb_delta=%.6f\n", delta / 1000000; if (delta > 10000) print "flag for review: source byte delta exceeds 10000" }'
acceptance.expected: After the final implementation commit, command exits 0 and reports BASE source size 1683 bytes (literal from the recorded base), HEAD source size, their difference in bytes, and that difference divided by 1e6 as estimated image_mb delta. The plan estimates +1000 to +3500 bytes, or +0.001 to +0.0035 MB; flag a delta above 10000 bytes for review. HEAD size is an observed measurement, not a test oracle. Read the protected Dockerfile and .dockerignore: Dockerfile copies src into the final image, while test/docs are absent. Scope check proves no other src file, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, dependency or lockfile changed, so this is the whole image content delta. Do not claim image contents or image_mb are unchanged; do not build an image or run the Docker bench (#834). Static import in src/index.ts means parsing a few KB more at service startup, expected within measurement noise; do not claim a measured startup improvement.

The PR body lists every added comment line, or says none if grep exits 1 with no matches. The new test file has no comments except optionally one top line naming the class and expected outcome. Source comments are limited to the accurate existing runSubscribers doc comment, one classifier-constant line naming SQLite primary codes and one escaping-helper doc line naming the escaped set. Preserve unrelated existing comments.

acceptance.command:
ALLOWED='README.md
docs/operation.md
src/subscribers-cli.ts
test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts'
PROTECTED='src/subscriber-store.ts src/index.ts src/failed-cli.ts src/ledger-lock.ts src/ledger.ts src/config.ts src/subscription-settings.ts src/channels/message.ts test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts test/subscriptions-support.ts package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml biome.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js lefthook.yml Dockerfile .dockerignore .github AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md docs/troubleshooting.md docs/configuration.md'
check_scope() {
  test "$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort)" = "$ALLOWED" &&
  git diff --exit-code "$BASE" HEAD -- $PROTECTED &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only --cached)" &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only)" &&
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" &&
  git diff --check "$BASE" HEAD
}
check_scope

All explicit protected paths have no BASE-to-HEAD diff. The index and worktree diffs are separately empty, status including untracked files is empty, and committed whitespace check passes.
